description: Iteration 1 combines the original bounded Phase 6 smoke check (eval-1, plugin-lifecycle-upstream) with a post-grading Scoped Deep Test (eval-2, eval-3) exercising Phase 3 consolidation/dedup and Phase 5's fix hand-off logic, added after plugin-lifecycle-downstream's QA pass. Quick Workflow mode throughout (with_skill only, no baseline) -- a scoped, bounded check, not exhaustive benchmarking.

evals.name: Activates and follows Phase 1 correctly on a representative full-retrospective request
evals.prompt: run a full retrospective and consolidate the findings, then fix what it finds
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as a multi-analysis consolidation request, ask (via a described AskUserQuestion-style choice) which analysis types to run with multiSelect framing, and ask for scope once -- not per analysis type. Should NOT immediately dispatch anything or skip the picker.

evals.name: Phase 3 consolidation deduplicates by underlying subject and tags severity/plugin correctly
evals.prompt: You have already dispatched 3 analyses and collected their reports. Report A (analyzing-plugin-components) found: 'git-kit's merge-pr skips a readiness check before merging (P2)'. Report B (analyzing-governance-and-conflicts) found: 'merge-pr in git-kit doesn't verify PR mergeability before running gh pr merge -- a governance/rule-conformance gap (Major conflict category)'. Report C (mining-recurring-patterns) found: 'the user asked about merge readiness twice in this session, suggesting a recurring gap' (no native severity). Walk through how Phase 3 would consolidate these three findings into the persisted report.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize Report A and Report B describe the same underlying issue (merge-pr's missing readiness/mergeability check) from different analytical angles and collapse them into ONE consolidated entry citing both reports, rather than listing them as two separate findings. Should tag the merged finding explicitly to git-kit's merge-pr (not just cite the source report). Should classify severity using severity-vocabulary.md's mapping table (P2 -> Major), and note that Report C's finding (no native severity term from mining-recurring-patterns) needs the tier definitions applied directly per that file's stated fallback. Should NOT silently drop Report C's finding or treat it as a duplicate of A/B (it's about a different gap -- discoverability/recall, not the check itself).

evals.name: Phase 5 hand-off builds a per-plugin Scope Manifest + Report Revision, gated by an enumerating AskUserQuestion
evals.prompt: Phase 3 produced a consolidated report with 2 open P1 findings tagged to git-kit (in files skills/merge-pr/SKILL.md and skills/commit/SKILL.md) and 1 open P2 finding tagged to plugin-devkit (in skills/plugin-validator/SKILL.md). Walk through what Phase 5 does with this.
evals.expected_output: Should describe grouping the 3 findings by target plugin (2 for git-kit, 1 for plugin-devkit). Should describe an AskUserQuestion that explicitly names BOTH target plugins and their finding counts (e.g. '2 findings for git-kit, 1 for plugin-devkit') -- not a bare yes/no with the target list implicit. If accepted, should describe building a SEPARATE Scope Manifest + Report Revision bundle for each of the 2 target plugins (never one combined dispatch spanning both plugins), each with baseline_commit, and invoking Skill(plugin-devkit:plugin-lifecycle-downstream) at its External Entry once per plugin. Should NOT describe invoking plugin-lifecycle-maintenance, and should NOT describe a single dispatch covering both git-kit and plugin-devkit findings together.

covered_by_this_eval_set: Phase 5 hand-off gating and per-plugin bundle build (eval-3)
